semantic_checks: The domain is a real normed vector space; finite dimension, completeness, Euclidean structure and analyticity of the norm are not assumed.
For nonzero v, the actual line t maps to t times v on the full symmetric interval |t|<r/||v|| lies in the radius-r ball. Its pullbacks of f and ||v|| times g are real analytic.
Norm homogeneity gives exactly f(tv)+|t| [||v|| g(tv)]=0. The previously reviewed absolute-value theorem applies on both sides of zero; ||v||>0 then removes its scalar factor.
Every nonzero point x in the ball is reached with v=x and t=1, with 1<r/||x|| proved. The center is handled using an independently chosen nonzero v and t=0.
Nontrivial E is explicit in the whole-ball theorem and is necessary: in the zero-dimensional space the norm term vanishes identically and g is unrestricted.
The conclusion is actual equality of both functions to zero on the entire open ball, not merely along a selected line or away from its center.
limits: This is a uniqueness theorem for an analytic-plus-norm decomposition about the norm singularity at zero. It provides no existence theorem for such decompositions.
